outcome: No result changing the classification of which finite groups are BI-groups (Babai invariant groups) was found in the window; the problem remains open with no case, bound, or resolution located.
summary: Babai's problem (posed by László Babai in 1979) asks which finite groups are BI-groups (Babai invariant groups): groups G such that whenever Cay(G,S) ≅ Cay(G,T) for inverse-closed connection sets, the character-sum multisets M_ν^S and M_ν^T agree for every irreducible character degree ν. The last substantive work on this exact question that I could find is Abdollahi and Zallaghi's 2015 'Character Sums for Cayley Graphs' (Comm. Algebra) and their 2017/2019 follow-up 'Non-abelian finite groups whose character sums are invariant but are not Cayley isomorphism' (arXiv:1710.04446, J. Algebra Appl. 2019), which exhibited non-abelian BI-groups of orders 20 and 42 that are not CI-groups and classified BI-groups up to order 30 — all before the 26 January 2024 frozen revision. I ran searches for 'BI-group', 'Babai invariant group', and combinations with 'character sum', 'Cayley graph', and years 2024-2026, and found no paper, preprint, or announcement addressing this classification question in the window. Adjacent-sounding hits are all out of scope under §3.1: 'bi-Cayley graphs' and 'm-BCI-groups' (e.g. the 2025 Communications in Algebra paper on generalized quaternion groups) concern isomorphism of a structurally different graph class (bi-Cayley graphs, built from two group copies) and the separate BCI-group property, not character-sum invariance of ordinary Cayley graphs. I also found that 'Babai's conjecture' — a well-studied, actively-progressing diameter bound for Cayley graphs of finite simple groups (with 2022-2025 partial results by various authors on transvections, classical groups, and random generators) — is a different problem sharing Babai's name; it is not a case or variant of the BI-group question and is out of scope. The Wikipedia article itself (as of my fetch) cites nothing after 2019 and shows no edits reflecting new results. I conclude nothing has happened to this specific problem in the window, and no AI system is implicated in any relevant work.
competing_reading: None of the adjacent literature (bi-Cayley/BCI-group papers, Babai's diameter conjecture, general Cayley isomorphism/CI-group work) plausibly constitutes even a narrow case of the BI-group classification question, so there is little ambiguity here; the main risk is a paper using different terminology (e.g. calling character-sum invariance something else) that my searches missed.
what_would_settle_it: A paper or preprint dated after 26 January 2024 that explicitly determines BI-group status (in the character-sum-invariance sense) for a new group, family of groups, or order range, or that proves/disproves BI-group status is equivalent to some other known group property.
